There's a lot of old discussion about damage effects and the order in which they are applied, but I still find the situation murky.  In particular, I'm not sure which of the old discussions have been overruled by later rulings.  (I always get suspicious when a thread starts talking about Imbued Fire/Flesh of the Sun God, which has since been ruled not to work.)

So here are some questions.

(1) Do damage-type-changing effects take place in the order in which cards are played?  For instance, if Ra's "Imbued Fire" is played before Visionary's "Twist the Ether", I would think the damage gets converted to fire, then to whatever Visionary chooses, while if "Twist the Ether" was played first, I would think the damage is always fire.  Is this correct?  I did find some people confused in other threads.

(2) When do damage bonuses get applied?  For instance, suppose Absolute Zero (AZ) and Ra are out. AZ has played Focused Apertures before Ra played Imbued Fire, and then AZ deals some cold damage.  Perhaps the cold damage gets the +1 from focused apertures, then is converted to fire by Imbued fire, then gets the +1 from Imbued Fire; or perhaps the damage type is computed first (and is fire), then there's only the one +1 from Imbued Fire.

(3) When AZ would deal cold damage to himself that is converted into healing by Null-Point Calibration Unit, does this count as cold damage dealt by AZ for the purposes of (eg) Thermal Shockwave?

(4) Can damage reduction get applied multiple times?  Eg, say Haka has Ta Moko out, and Legacy has Lead from the Front and Fortitude out.  Then a villain deals damage to Haka.  Can this get reduced by 1 by Ta Moko, switched to Legacy by Lead from the Front, then reduced by 1 by Fortitude?  Does it depend on the order the cards were played in?

(5) For effects like Fanatic's Undaunted, when do I check the damage amount?

(Text: "Whenever exactly 1 damage would be dealt to Fanatic, prevent that damage. Whenever Fanatic would be dealt 5 or more damage from a single source, reduce that damage by 2.")

(6) In general, I'd like to see an accounting of the precise steps involved in computing damage.  I suspect the answers to (2) and (4) are both "no, that combo doesn't work", but why not?  One algorithm I would know how to apply would be to have virtual damage floating around, modified by all cards played in the order they were played (damage increased/decreased, targets switched, type changed, converted to healing, etc.)  But I gather this is not the algorithm?

I'm with Ameena on TtE.  Also environment cards that change things universally, I believe that TtE's effect is activated after the universal, non-optional effects, because it is optional, it would be wierd if you would have to decide what damage and whether to increase it before checking all the other steps.

Its taken me a while to get used to the flow of calculations because I'm used to CCGs and the method of applying effects they have.

This game has its own, and it is quite different, but also quite intuitive once you get the hang of it, or at least most of the time.

Damage reduction is personal, damage increases like focused Aperature and imbued fire only apply to their element.

So if Imbued fire and focused aperature are out and AZ has Twist the Ether on himself and he tries to cold himself the cold damage would be increased by aperature, except that it isn't cold damage, Imbued fire has made it fire, and raised it by it's own effect.  So AZ's ability to deal himelf fire or cold has become fire or fire.  Then I believe Visionary can change that through TtE, since it's effect is activated after imbued fire has done it's thing.  IF Vis changes that damage to Cold, it loses the +1 from imbued fire and regains the +1 from aperature, as well as Vis's effect of raising or lowering it.  If she changes it to Radiant, Melee or Fluffy Bunny damage, the other bonuses don't apply and only her own effect can raise or lower it.  (Fluffy Bunny damage is unstable and I wouldn't suggest using it)

For damage done, the target has to actually take damage, which I believe means that if a target has two health and you hit them for 4 health you only get credit for two.  The exception to this is if they are indestructible, under those circumstances it is official that targets can enter negative HP, which means you can deal damage past 0hp.

The steps would seem to be:

1.  the starting step that leads to damage being dealt.

2.  Check for any modifiers to damage from that target.  If damage changes type re-check.

3.  Check for redirection.

4.  Check for modifiers to damage dealt to target.

5.  Calculate final damage, check for immunity, negation or change to healing.

6.  Check for redirection, if redirected return to step 4.

7.  Apply damage.

8.  Check for destruction and effects

9.  Check for retaliation effects.

I don't think I missed anything.  Feel free to add points if I did.

Interesting note, AZ's cold to healing is not changing the damage type, you don't lose the modifiers to cold damage dealt or taken, you just heal for the amount you would be damaged, I honestly don't know if you would gain universal increases to recovery or not, we do in my group, but I don't know officially.

We just had this TtE and Imbued Fire combo in our last game.  Imbued Fire is a constant effect so I believe the order is something like:

1) Player does X melee damage.

2) Melee is converted to fire and increased to X+1 as a result of Imbued Fire.

3) TtE is used to convert the damage to say energy and increased by one.  Damage is now energy and no longer gets the IF bonus, so it's energy X+1.

4) IF is a constant effect.  The damage is immediately converted back to fire, and the IF fire increase now applies again.  The damage is now X+2 fire.

X + 1 from TtE + 1 from IF.

I don't think you can use the text on TtE more than once for a single damage source.  This would mean that whatever type you change to is overridden by any constant effects.  If TtE didn't operate that way then you could change the damage type and amount every time the type was changed by a constant effect causing an infinite loop of damage increases.  I think, I don't have the card in front of me.

The real sticky situation is Imbued Fire coupled with an environment card that converts all damage.  I assume in that situation it's down to card play order.

To clarify, when I say that Imbued Fire is constant effect, I mean it in the sense that it does not have a conditional trigger in order to apply the effect. The effect is triggered only by playing the card, and the effect takes hold. 

Any global damage type modifiers that come into play post Imbued Fire would override it due to order of cards played as the effects are contradictory. So if Close Quarters Combat (all damage to melee) or Irradiated Vat (all damage to Toxic) comes out after Imbued Fire, they take precedence.

Twist the Ether is a very different kind of manipulation than any of those above. Yes, they all change the damage type. But they have very different triggers. Where Imbued Fire's effect is triggered upon it being played, Twist the Ether triggers as a hero is attacking (and it is an optional trigger for the player). There are many official rulings about how to resolve triggered effects. They all that if you have multiple conditional triggers trying to resolve, the newest trigger takes precedence over the old ones. Thats why you can use Bee Bot to destroy End of Days before it burns all of the Heros things. Same principle. Twist the Ether, whos effect has to be triggered (therefor being a newer triggered effect than IF), will override Imbued Fire's damage type restriction. But you can still benefit from the +1 damage from IF as long as you keep using fire damage with TtE

So, the interpretation is that the damage type alteration of TtE is always the last on the stack so to speak.  All global effects are applied in play order followed by TtE.

Spiff's rules clarifications for Imbued Fire say:

Both parts of the text on Imbued Fire ("Increase all fire damage by 1.", and "Change the damage type of damage dealt by hero targets to fire.") are ongoing, static buffs.  These things aren't happening in any order because it's not a power or one-shot, so once it's in play, both of the effects are in play simultaneously, which would play out like so:

All fire damage is increased by one, okay.  Change the damage type of damage dealt by heroes to fire.  Now I'm dealing fire damage, but wait, all fire damage is plus one.  So yes, Imbued Fire gives everyone an increased one damage.

(I typed that in and didn't copy-paste so please forgive any errors.)

This implies that those static effects are always in effect.  Otherwise nobody gets a +1 to damage from Imbued Fire for attacks that are changed to fire since the attack wasn't fire when the damage increase went off.

The problem with making an "algorithim" is that there are so many little interactions that give rise to so many edge cases it would be extremely hard to get a solid one down. For consecutive triggers and overlapping effects, the newest triggered effects take precedance over older ones.

FWIW, here's my algorithm:

Given the source of an attack, the destination of an attack (target), the type  of an attack, and the amount of an attack:
 
  1. Apply all cards that affect the type of the attack in card played order. (This is only done as an separate, first step, because there are no cards which change the type of an attack based on either the destination of the attack or the amount of the attack, and there are no cards which change the source of an attack).
  2. Apply all other cards in card played order. If a card changes the destinatio n of the attack (target), reset the amount of the attack to the original amount  and return to the beginning of this step, but don't consider that card again. 
  3. If the attack is 0 or less or the target is immune, no damage is dealt.
 
Other relevant rules and effects:
  • An attack that has been reduced to zero or less can NOT be  redirected.
  • Stored increase (Haka of Battle) or reduction (Wraith's Stealth)  are applied in card played order as well.
  • There is no established order of the hero and villain character cards, so I would let that be a player decision, if it ever came up. Another thought would be to say the order is the order of turns, so villain character cards first followed by each hero character card.
 

Basically, card played order is King. Some perhaps non-intuitive results can occur. For instance, if Mr. Fixer is hitting himself due to an Infection and has a plus one from a tool and a plus one from Harmony, whether or not he can redirect due to Praying Mantis is going to depend on the order in which his cards were played. Praying Mantis before one or both of the tool and Harmony? Amount is one or two, so redirection! After both? Amount is three, so not redirected.

It is not a constant effect, there are effects that cover a period of time, like immunity and indestructibility.  You are right that Imbued fire changes the damage type to fire.

This does not allow for boosting a single instance of damage as both projectile and fire.  Because it cannot be both projectile and fire.

Damage reduction does not carry in redirection, because it only protects the target that has it, if damage going to Tachyon is reduced, then redirected to a target that isn't covered by the reduction Tachyon has, then the damage is not reduced by that reduction.  Same with Micro Targetting computer and imbued fire, whenever the damage type is changed conditional modifiers have to be reevaluated, in case the condition of the modification is no longer applicable.

As a point that is a bit away from the discussion, and to repeat my earlier stance:  I believe that optional modifiers like TTE can be applied at will within the time frame of their activation.  If TTE is played, then Imbued fire, then close quarters combat, when the hero with TTE sitting next to their card would deal damage it is changed to fire and then melee, throughout that process it is still in the "would be dealt damage" phase, and I would say that Visionary could choose to wait until both had triggered and resolved before activating the effect of TTE, still in proper timing, since it is still the "would be dealt damage" timing.

The best sense of an order we have is the text "would deal damage" vs. "Deals damage", (or be dealt if it's defensive)  I posted what I think is a pretty good resolution order, I seperated the damage type and amount modifers, simply because it makes it easier to keep straight. I'll repost it here:

1:  Damage Declaration, initial Source, type, amount and target are declared.

2:  Apply changes to damage type.

3:  Apply modifiers to damage based on source and type.

4:  Source of damage steps complete, check for redirection based on source, proceed to target.

5.  If target is immune end damage calculations, no damage is dealt.

6.  Trigger all "would be dealt damage" reduction and redirection effects.

7.  Trigger all "is dealt damage" modifiers.

8,  Reduce targets HP.

Step 5 exists because of an official ruling that you can't redirect damage that the hero is immune to, since they could not be dealt that damage.  Officially inside each step you should go by card order, although on steps 6 and 7 I tend to let the heroes choose the order, because it gets annoying to keep track of which cards were played first, and arguments don't improve the game when someone misremembers.

Thinking in terms of a 1) Cards effect and 2) How that effect triggers is the best way to look at this game in general.

If there are triggered effects that happen simultaniously (like multiple end of turn triggered effects for example) then card order matters. Any other time and card order has no impact. 

Attack modifications are not simultanious, unless they are part of a trigger condition for that effect. For instance, Legacy has Surge of Strength and Inspiring Presence. Both are attack modifications of +1 damage. Now if we read the card, there is no condition that must be met to activate that +1 damage (in other words, nothing like "if X happens, do Y" where X is the trigger condition and Y is the effect). It can be understood then that the trigger for the effect is the act of playing the card. Once you play a card like Surge of Strength, the triggered effect now takes hold and all Legacy's damage is increased by 1. Since there is no explicit end point listed on the card, it is understood that the effect is consistant as long as the card remains in play. 

Back to Imbued Fire and Micro Targeting Computer/Razor Ordinance. Lets break down these 3 cards in terms of card effects and the triggers for those effects.

Imbued Fire. Increase all fire damage from heros by 1. Like SoS, there is no conditional trigger, so the effect triggers instantly upon playing, and because there is nothing limiting the duration of the effect, it is constant as long as the card remains in play. The effect has a limitation however in that the damage delt needs to be fire. The second part changes all hero damage to fire type. This is also an effect with no conditional trigger or expressed end point so it behaves the same way.

Micro Targeting Computer says to increase projectile damage delt by Wraith by 2. Like SoS there is no conditional trigger for the effect, so it happens instantly upon playing it. MTC also has a limitation similar to the first part of Imbued Fire in that that damage delt must be projectile.

Razor Ordinace has a Power. During a Heros power phase, that hero my activate one Power, acting as the trigger condition for that Power's effect. Razor Ordinace lets you deal 3 projectile damage to one target.

Let's say that all 3 of these cards are in play during a particular game. It's Wraiths turn and shes looking to do some damage. So Wraith needs to trigger an effect that deals damage. This is where the first big distinction comes in. Razor Ordinance must be triggered after the effects of IF and MTC are in play.

Lets read the Power. Wraith deals one target 3 projectile damage. If you read the power like this, you have already made a mistake. Imbued Fire is already changing all hero damage to fire. So as you are reading her powers and deciding what to use, you would not even read the word "projectile" as you are replacing it with "Fire" the instant Imbued Fire hits the field. That is the second big distinction. You can't trigger the effect of Razor Ordinance before Imbued Fire has already changed the damage type.

Now Wraith chooses to use that power, so she triggers that power's effect. Now that she is dealing fire damage, she is within the other effect of Imbued Fire and increases that fire damage by 1. 

It makes no difference whether or not MTC or IF were in play first. Why? For starters, the two effects we are specifically looking at here (the +2 projectile damage and the change all damage to fire) are not simultaniously triggered, so there is the first big tip off. The other big reason here is the fact that if a hero, at any time, fails to meet the criteria for an effect, they loose that effect. Even if you thought the +2 projectile damage is applied before Imbued Fire changes the type, as soon as Wraith is no longer dealing projectile damge, MTC stops buffing as well since you no longer meet the criteria to benefit from it (that criteria being doing projectile damage).

Destruction at 0hp is a constant, passive effect.  It does have a trigger, just like anything changing damage has a trigger.  One-shots are activated when they enter play, the triggering effect is the card entering play.  If it does not enter play the effect does not occur, if it does enter play the effect occurs, the action that causes the effect to happen is called a trigger.

Infinite loops like that are not an intended part of the game. That is a no brainer. The question becomes, how do we interpret card interactions knowing that.

We talked a lot about the infinite redirection combos that could turn up with cards like Smoke Bombs and Stealth Bot. And the forum consensus at the time was that allowing 1 instance of redirection per 1 instance of damage was a comfortable solution to keep all the functionality of redirection intact but make infinite loops essentially impossible.

This is easily addressed with a Smoke Bomb example. Lets say all the heros are tied for HP (so they are all the highest and lowest HP hero) and Blade Batallion is dealing 3 damage to someone. Smoke Bombs redirects from hero A to hero B and decreases the damage by 1. Now, hero B is also the lowest target. Should Smoke Bombs be allowed to redirect that instance of damage again? Saying no seems like the simplest solution here. Even if you could still redirect in this situation, remember that damage mods reset every time you redirect. So if you redirect damage from B now to C, Batallion would still do hero C 2 damage (as you are not allowed to double dip the Smoke Bomb debuff, as that would lead to an infinite damage reduction loop, which, again, is surely not an intended aspect of gameplay). So in the above situation, why wouldn't you have just chosen C with the first redirect anyway if hero C will essentially take the same damage regardless of how many times Smoke Bombs bounces it around.

This does not have any official ruling as far as I am aware, but it is an elegant solution to address this particular problem.
